name: Kendall

high_schools.name: Miami Killian Senior High School
high_schools.note: Zoned high school for much of central Kendall, 10655 SW 97th Ave

high_schools.name: Felix Varela Senior High School
high_schools.note: Serves the Hammocks and West Kendall area

training_venues.name: Kendale Lakes Park
training_venues.note: County park with confirmed outdoor basketball, tennis, and racquetball courts plus a recreation center running youth basketball programs

local_paragraph: Kendall is less one neighborhood than a whole stretch of southwest Miami-Dade, and asking where someone lives usually gets an answer built around cross streets, 88th Street or 137th Avenue, rather than a name. Killian and Varela split the area's basketball talent, each pulling players from a different corner of the sprawl. Kendale Lakes Park, off 142nd Avenue, keeps its hoops busy most evenings once homework wraps up, alongside tennis and racquetball courts under the same roof. Dadeland Mall marks the unofficial northern edge, a reference point locals use even for directions nowhere near the mall itself. Coaching a Kendall kid means planning around whichever stretch of the Turnpike he crosses that day, since a session that ignores commute time gets skipped more than one that plans for it.
meta_description: Private basketball skills training for Kendall boys 11 to 18, built around Killian and Varela schedules, from a coach who evaluated college recruits.

name: Pinecrest

high_schools.name: Miami Palmetto Senior High School
high_schools.note: Zoned high school for the Village of Pinecrest, 7431 SW 120th St

training_venues.name: Suniland Park
training_venues.note: Ten acre village park with confirmed outdoor basketball courts alongside baseball and football fields

local_paragraph: Pinecrest carries itself like a small town tucked inside Miami-Dade, oak canopy over Red Road and a village government still arguing about tree ordinances. Palmetto pulls talent from the whole village and beyond, and its gym anchors most of the local basketball conversation. A short walk from the middle school of the same name, Suniland Park keeps its hoops full most afternoons, tucked a block off South Dixie Highway near the old Suniland shopping strip. Pinecrest Gardens draws an entirely different crowd, families there for the farmers market rather than a jump shot. A player already committed to the varsity roster still needs individual reps a team practice cannot supply on its own, which is where the extra work tends to happen.
meta_description: Private basketball training near Suniland Park for Pinecrest players 11 to 18, scheduled around Palmetto Panthers practice and school demands.

name: Coral Gables

high_schools.name: Coral Gables Senior High School
high_schools.note: City of Coral Gables zoned high school, 450 Bird Rd, home of the Cavaliers

training_venues.name: Coral Gables War Memorial Youth Center
training_venues.note: Confirmed 13,244 square foot indoor gymnasium plus outdoor lighted basketball courts, membership required for youth center access

local_paragraph: Coral Gables is a city of coral rock arches and roundabouts, and Coral Gables Senior High sits right on Bird Road, close enough to the Biltmore that visiting families sometimes confuse the two landmarks. The War Memorial Youth Center on University Drive has both an indoor gym and lighted outdoor courts, making it one of the few Gables venues that works rain or shine. Miracle Mile is a few blocks north, useful shorthand when describing where a gym sits relative to downtown. Families here tend to be scheduling around Ponce de Leon Middle and a packed after school calendar, so training sessions get built around whatever window actually exists that week rather than an ideal one that never shows up.
meta_title: Coral Gables Basketball Training | Fast Basketball
meta_description: Private basketball training for Coral Gables families at War Memorial Youth Center, built around Cavaliers practice and a packed school week.

training_venues.name: Tropical Park
training_venues.note: Large county park with confirmed outdoor basketball courts, a short drive northeast of Westchester proper

local_paragraph: Westchester is one of the older, more built out corners of unincorporated Miami-Dade, tight single family blocks stacked between Bird Road and Coral Way. Coral Park has been the neighborhood's basketball address for generations, a program alumni still bring up decades later at family gatherings. Miller Drive Park, tucked off 94th Court near Rockway Middle, fills its basketball, tennis, and pickleball courts once the bell rings for the day. A few minutes northeast on 40th Street, Tropical Park adds another option for a family willing to make the short drive. Because Westchester is dense and every side street eventually dead ends into a bigger road, Fast Basketball plans a route before picking a venue, not after.
meta_description: Private basketball training for Westchester players 11 to 18 at Miller Drive Park, scheduled around Coral Park High practice and travel time.

name: Doral

high_schools.note: Zoned high school for the City of Doral, 8600 NW 107th Ave

training_venues.name: Doral Central Park
training_venues.note: Confirmed outdoor basketball courts inside a larger city sports complex

local_paragraph: Doral did not exist as its own city until 2003, and the construction cranes along 107th Avenue make clear it has not stopped growing since. Doral High anchors much of the area's basketball scene near where 107th meets the Palmetto Expressway. Nearby, Doral Central Park stretches across 92nd Avenue with enough acreage for baseball diamonds, a dog park, and a set of hoops that rarely sit empty on a weekday evening. CityPlace Doral gives visitors a landmark to navigate by when a court is a few turns off the main road. Doral pulls kids from dozens of countries and just as many club sports calendars, so Fast Basketball asks about a full week before building a plan instead of assuming a blank schedule.
meta_description: Private basketball skills training for Doral players 11 to 18 at Doral Central Park, built around Doral Senior High practice and club conflicts.

local_paragraph: Miami Lakes still has the small town feel its planners intended, with Main Street as the obvious center and Miami Lakes Educational Center serving much of the area's high school population. Miami Lakes Optimist Park, off NW 162nd Street, has four outdoor courts that get steady traffic from Miami Lakes Middle kids right after the bell. Royal Oaks Park sits nearby too, a quieter option on weekends. Because Miami Lakes borders both Hialeah and the Palmetto Expressway corridor, families here often want a coach willing to work early mornings before the commute gets bad. Fast Basketball schedules around that reality instead of asking Miami Lakes parents to fight afternoon traffic to reach a gym across town.

local_paragraph: Palmetto Bay runs along Old Cutler Road, shaded and slower paced than the suburbs just north of it, with Coral Reef Senior High serving as the area's main feeder into college recruiting conversations. Palmetto Bay Park, on SW 95th Avenue, has basketball and pickleball courts that share space with a skate park and two playgrounds. Southwood Middle sits a short drive west, and its dismissal time shapes a lot of family schedules in the village. Fast Basketball works with Palmetto Bay families who want their son seen by the same kind of eye that used to sit in the stands evaluating recruits, without turning a Tuesday evening into a fight through rush hour traffic on US-1.

training_venues.name: Founders Park
training_venues.note: Outdoor basketball court completed November 2024, converted from a former tennis court

local_paragraph: Aventura is compact and vertical, condo towers stacked along Biscayne Boulevard with Aventura Mall as the landmark everyone already knows. Don Soffer Aventura High School opened relatively recently on NE 213th Street and has quickly become the center of the area's basketball conversation. Founders Park, just off NE 190th Street, added an outdoor basketball court in 2024, giving the city courts that did not exist a few years earlier. Families here are often balancing a school day at Aventura City of Excellence with club commitments across the county line in Broward. Fast Basketball treats Aventura as its own pocket of the service area, with sessions timed around the Waterways traffic pattern rather than a one size schedule that ignores it.
meta_description: Private basketball training for Aventura players 11 to 18 near Don Soffer Aventura High, scheduled around club ball and a tight school day.

name: Weston

high_schools.note: Zoned high school for most of Weston, 18600 Vista Park Blvd

training_venues.name: Weston Regional Park
training_venues.note: Confirmed eight outdoor lighted basketball courts, free to use

local_paragraph: Weston sits west of the Everglades levee, planned and orderly, with Cypress Bay High School serving as the largest single feeder of basketball talent in the city. Weston Regional Park, on Saddle Club Road, has eight outdoor basketball courts, more than almost anywhere else in this part of Broward, and they stay busy through the evening. Tequesta Trace Middle and Falcon Cove Middle split the city's younger players between them. Bonaventure gives longtime residents a shorthand for the western half of town. Fast Basketball works with Weston families around a school and club schedule that is often already full, adding a focused skill session rather than one more full length scrimmage to an already long week.
meta_description: Private basketball training for Weston families near Cypress Bay High and Weston Regional Park, built around an already full school week.

local_paragraph: Pembroke Pines is one of Broward's biggest cities by population, stretching from Flamingo Road almost to the Everglades levee on the west side. Flanagan alone sends dozens of players a year into some level of college ball, drawing kids from well outside its immediate zone. C.B. Smith Park, better known locally for its water park than for basketball, still keeps courts busy along North Flamingo Road most weekday evenings. Walter C. Young feeds the high school roster years in advance, while Pines Middle, closer to Douglas Road on the east side, sends players a different direction entirely. A city this large means two Pembroke Pines addresses can be twenty minutes apart, so Fast Basketball confirms where a kid actually lives before deciding which end of town to meet him in.
meta_title: Pembroke Pines Basketball Training | Fast Basketball
meta_description: Private basketball training for Pembroke Pines players 11 to 18 near C.B. Smith Park, scheduled around Flanagan practice and travel ball.

local_paragraph: Miramar sits right against the Miami-Dade line, close enough that plenty of residents work north of the county border and drive home against traffic every evening. The high school on 89th Avenue has quietly sent players into college programs for years without much outside attention. A short trip down Miramar Parkway, the regional park spreads basketball courts across a much bigger complex the city expanded gradually over two decades. New Renaissance and Glades split the youngest players between two different feeder patterns on opposite sides of town. Because so many parents here are still driving home from Miami-Dade at five o'clock, Fast Basketball leaves room in the evening rather than assuming everyone is free the second school lets out.

local_paragraph: Cooper City markets itself as the place families move to on purpose, not just where they end up, and the high school on Stirling Road backs up that reputation with one of the stronger athletic programs in western Broward. Just over the city line on Sheridan Street, Brian Piccolo hosts soccer fields, a velodrome, and a couple of basketball hoops most residents already visit for reasons that have nothing to do with the sport. Pioneer feeds directly into the varsity roster a few years down the line, so younger players here are usually thinking two steps ahead already. A plan that competes with an already packed practice calendar gets dropped fast, so sessions get built to sit alongside it instead.
